question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class outbound recipient allowlist for Slack DMs, and should that policy be Slack-local or a shared channel/Gateway contract?
rationale: The request adds a public security-hardening config surface and must settle enforcement scope, defaults, and how it fits the documented trusted-operator model before implementation.

options.title: Approve explicit outbound target policy
options.body: Add `allowTo`-style outbound recipient authorization with compatible defaults and shared enforcement coverage across CLI, Gateway, message-tool, and Slack send paths.

options.title: Fold into broader outbound guardrails
options.body: Defer this focused Slack request to the broader human-chat outbound policy and verified-delivery design in #87870.

options.title: Decline as trusted-operator scope
options.body: Keep `allowFrom` inbound-only and rely on operator trust, tool policy, and agent instructions for outbound sends.

recommendation.title: Approve explicit outbound target policy
recommendation.body: Add `allowTo`-style outbound recipient authorization with compatible defaults and shared enforcement coverage across CLI, Gateway, message-tool, and Slack send paths.

likelyOwner.reason: This person authored the prior security-boundary triage and has adjacent outbound policy history, making them the best available owner for the product/security call.
